Medulloblastoma: Noncontrast CT of the head showed no abnormalities
GRE T2* sequences showed no hemorrhage or calcification
Chief complaint: 4-month history of severe occipital and temporal headaches
Headaches were paroxysmal, aggravated by changes in position
Associated symptoms: bilateral blurry vision and morning projectile vomiting
Neurological examination showed kinetic and static cerebellar syndrome
Cerebellar syndrome included ataxia, imbalance, uncoordinated movements, bilateral nystagmus, and stage I bilateral papilledema
Brain MRI revealed an inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis measuring 40 × 31 × 29 mm
Lesion was hypointense on T1-weighted images
Lesion was heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images
Lesion showed heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration
Lesion filled the foramen of Magendie and exerted mass effect on the medulla
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy showed an elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal
